A restatement, at implementation precision, of what the parent authority already ratified for CE-1 (COMMERCIAL_ACCOUNT.target_shape, ORGANIZATION_RELATION.live_association, CC-1, CC-4, SEC-2, SEC-7, PG-1, PG-3) — narrowed from the parent's DERIVED_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION-level shape to concrete column types, defaults, constraints and index kind.

NOT a re-opening of the parent authority's MIGRATION_DAG, SECURITY_CONTROLS, MUTATION_CONTROLS or REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTRACT. CE-1's entries there control; this document narrows them to implementation precision and adds nothing that contradicts them.

CA_VERBATIM_CONSUMED.CA-02: One CommercialAccount may govern one or more Organizations.
CA_VERBATIM_CONSUMED.CA-05: Stripe/payment state does not directly grant application authorization.
CA_VERBATIM_CONSUMED.CA-06: An Organization is governed by exactly one CommercialAccount at a time. A governed transfer, Platform-Admin-initiated in Commercial V1, may change that association without altering the Organization id, tenant data, memberships, roles, evidence, or audit history. The pre-transfer CommercialAccount association must remain historically reconstructible. Entitlements must be explicitly re-evaluated under the receiving CommercialAccount rather than silently inherited from the prior one. This does not ratify any specific schema table or FK design — a live-FK-plus-history-relation is a derived architecture recommendation, not product doctrine.
CA_VERBATIM_CONSUMED.CA-07: CommercialAccount owns the commercial/payment relationship: Stripe customer/subscription/price identity and plan/catalog identity. Effective EntitlementGrants, usage meters and quota enforcement remain scoped to Organization x product-capability per CA-04. CommercialAccount-level plan state defines what an Organization may be entitled to but is never itself evaluated as tenant authorization.

ORGANIZATION_FK.constraint: NULLABLE, NO DEFAULT, NO CE-1 BACKFILL

fk.rationale: RESTRICT (not CASCADE, not SET NULL) is the DERIVED_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION this mission freezes: a CommercialAccount that still governs a live Organization must not be deletable at all — deleting the governing account out from under a live Organization is exactly the kind of silent-loss-of-commercial-identity the parent authority's reconstructibility requirements (CA-06, SEC-12) are designed to prevent. A CommercialAccount may only be removed after every Organization it governs has been transferred (CE-2) or the FK cleared.

index.convention_citation: Mirrors the existing per-FK index pattern already used for every other organization_id-shaped FK in this schema, e.g. db/schema.ts:84-85 (idx_audit_logs_organization_id) and :103-104 (idx_invitations_organization_id).

ORGANIZATION_FK.nullable_meaning: NULL means 'no CommercialAccount governs this Organization' per parent ORGANIZATION_RELATION.ungoverned_state. It is set by NO writer at CE-1 — no default, no backfill (CE-4's job), no trigger. Every existing Organization row has this column NULL immediately after CE-1 lands, and that is the entire intended effect of this node on the table.

SECURITY.classification: EXECUTABLE_SECURITY_POSTURE derived from parent SEC-2, SEC-7, PG-1, PG-3.
frozen: CREATE TABLE commercial_accounts is followed, in the same migration, by ALTER TABLE commercial_accounts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; and ALTER TABLE commercial_accounts FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;.
ZERO CREATE POLICY statements are written against commercial_accounts at CE-1. No tenant-facing policy of any kind.

CommercialAccount is NOT tenant data (parent statement, restated verbatim: 'CommercialAccount is not tenant data'). No tenant role gains access merely from sharing the account. Platform Admin read/write capability belongs to later CE nodes (CE-8, per parent PLATFORM_ADMIN_BOUNDARY) and is explicitly NOT granted here.
SECURITY.why_force_and_zero_policies: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with zero policies denies every ordinary role by default (no policy = no match = deny). FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY additionally binds the table owner and any role with BYPASSRLS-independent superuser status is the only escape — meaning even a migration or application role that happens to own the table cannot read or write rows through ordinary DML once RLS is forced. This is the strongest available default-deny posture for a relation with no ratified tenant-facing access pattern at all, which is exactly CommercialAccount's status at CE-1.
SECURITY.novel_pattern_disclosure: Measured at AS_OF_HEAD by grep across db/migrations/*.sql: every existing ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY statement in this repository's application schema is immediately followed by one or more CREATE POLICY statements (e.g. db/migrations/0045_fib_domain_object_version_lineage.sql, 0048_fib_evidence_versions.sql, 0062_fib_methodological_assumptions.sql). commercial_accounts is the FIRST application table in this repository to combine ENABLE + FORCE with ZERO policies. This is a deliberate, mission-directed departure and not an oversight; it is recorded here so an implementing or auditing mission does not mistake it for a forgotten policy set.

PG_1.proves: SEC-7 — a subject scoped to OrgA reads zero rows of OrgB despite a shared CommercialAccount X.
PG_1.status_after_CE1: PARTIALLY GROUNDED. CE-1 makes SEC-7 hold TRIVIALLY for commercial_accounts itself (zero policies means no tenant reads the table at all, by any organization). SEC-7's harder claim — that organizations.commercial_account_id being shared does not widen a tenant RLS predicate over OTHER tables — is a property of every OTHER table's existing RLS policies, which CE-1 does not touch and does not need to touch, because CE-1 adds no RLS predicate anywhere that references commercial_account_id. A real-PostgreSQL probe (per parent REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTRACT.harness_shape: two-account, three-organization fixture) remains MANDATORY before CE-1 closes, to prove the negative — that nothing in the existing policy set was written to accidentally join through the new column.
PG_1.future_proof_required: Exhaustive grep of db/baseline/**/*.sql and db/migrations/**/*.sql for any existing RLS predicate that references organizations.commercial_account_id (there must be none, since the column does not yet exist at AS_OF_HEAD) PLUS a disposable-cluster probe confirming a scoped read of OrgA returns zero rows of a sibling OrgB governed by the same account.

PG_3.proves: commercial_accounts is not tenant-readable: a tenant principal scoped to OrgA cannot read account X's row, and cannot enumerate the sibling OrgB through it.
PG_3.status_after_CE1: This is CE-1's OWN probe (parent REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTRACT names node=CE-1 for PG-3). It is the direct runtime verification of the ENABLE+FORCE+zero-policy posture above. Static reading of the migration SQL is NOT proof — the parent's own rationale (RLS policy combination is a runtime property) applies with full force to a table with NO policies as much as to one with several: the mandatory probe must confirm that the tenant-facing application database role is NOT a member of any role with BYPASSRLS, and is NOT the table owner, or FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY provides no protection against it.
PG_3.future_proof_required: A disposable-cluster probe, run AS the tenant-facing runtime role (never as a migration/superuser role), attempting SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against commercial_accounts and asserting every one is denied. The role's BYPASSRLS and ownership status must be asserted, not assumed, because FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is silently inert for a BYPASSRLS role or the table owner.

MULTIORG_CP2.no_stale_base_blind_merge: Neither lane may merge its schema.ts/migrations diff against a base older than the other lane's latest integrated state without re-measuring. A three-way textual merge of two additive schema.ts diffs can be syntactically clean and still silently drop an index or constraint (parent SHARED_WRITERS.writers[path=db/schema.ts].collision: 'Textual merges here are silent'); the correct sequencing is serial landing with a rebase, not a merge of two concurrent branches.
